name: 4-morpholinecarbodithioic acid 4-morpholinyl ester
description: 4-Morpholinecarbodithioic acid 4-morpholinyl ester (CAS 13752-51-7 ), also known as morpholin-4-yl morpholine-4-carbodithioate, is a sulfur-based compound used in rubber and polymer processing. It functions as a curing and crosslinking agent by initiating and regulating vulcanization reactions. This contributes to controlled network formation in various elastomeric systems and industrial applications. In rubber compounding, it acts as an accelerator or co-accelerator during vulcanization. This helps to establish crosslink density and improve the mechanical performance of finished rubber goods. Tire manufacturers and industrial rubber product producers use it to fine-tune cure rates. This ensures consistent processing behavior across different compound batches during the manufacturing cycle. In polymer systems, it supports controlled radical or ionic polymerization initiation. This makes it relevant for specialty resin and adhesive formulations requiring specific chemical properties. It is also evaluated in heterocyclic compound research and development programs. These programs target new curing system designs to enhance the durability and stability of modern polymer materials. This compound is typically supplied as a solid powder or crystalline form suited for direct weighing. It is available primarily in technical grade with purity specifications varying by supplier. Packaging options generally range from laboratory quantities to bulk industrial supply depending on scale. Proper storage is required to maintain the chemical integrity of the product over time.
